diag.title: Diagnosis
diag.subtitle: Which tool uses which proxy?
diag.needsPx: px has to be installed and running. Start px above, then switch the tools to it.
diag.kerberosNote: npm, pip and most Node, Python, Go and Rust tools cannot do Kerberos. That is why they point to px, and px handles the sign-in.

hints.windows: Stays unchanged: px reads exactly this setting to find the company proxy.
hints.nuget: dotnet restore and Visual Studio read http_proxy and no_proxy from %APPDATA%\NuGet\NuGet.Config.
hints.vscode: Ember only changes "http.proxy" and "http.noProxy" in settings.json; comments and other entries stay.
hints.nodeCerts: Node.js, npm, npx and Playwright do not use the Windows certificate store. If the company proxy inspects TLS, downloads fail with “unable to get local issuer certificate”. “Set up” exports the trusted certificates from Windows to C:\Ember\Certs and sets NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS.
hints.env: NO_PROXY holds the internal domains, so git, npm, pip, Python and Node.js reach internal servers directly instead of going through px.
hints.git: For every internal domain Ember also sets http.<url>.proxy to empty and allowNTLMAuth to true. git then reaches internal servers directly and signs in with Windows, even while px is not running. NO_PROXY covers deeper subdomains.
hints.gitExceptionsMissing: These internal addresses still lack the exception or the Windows sign-in: {list}. “Point to px” adds them.
hints.pip: pip.ini has no exception list. pip reaches internal servers directly through NO_PROXY (environment variables row).
hints.powershell: Otherwise Windows PowerShell sends irm, iwr and WebClient to the proxy from the PAC file without signing in there, so installers like “irm … | iex” fail. Ember puts px into the profile of Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7 ({files}); internal domains go directly.
hints.powershellPolicy: The execution policy “{policy}” keeps Windows PowerShell from loading the profile: set it to RemoteSigned under System.

proxy.subtitle: External repositories (GitHub, npm registries, …) go through px. git reaches internal servers directly and with your Windows sign-in, since they are often not reachable through the company proxy.

proxy.signInValue: Windows sign-in (allowNTLMAuth) for the internal domains

create.title: New project from the Ember template

access.advancedHint: Ctrl + E hides and shows Power, AI and Permissions.

access.notFound: “{name}” does not exist in the directory.
access.unchecked: “{name}” could not be checked in the directory right now (VPN?) and was added as {kind}.
access.meHint: Your domain groups. Put a group straight into a role.
access.savedToast: Saved. Everybody else gets the roles the next time they start Ember.

problems.noTeamFile: Ember knows no team.json. Without it there are no roles: enter the path under Settings.
problems.teamOffline: team.json cannot be reached right now. You see the local copy; saving works again once connected.
problems.teamReadOnly: You may only read team.json ({path}). Saving needs write access to the file, which IT grants for the share.

locked.title: Ember is not enabled for you yet
locked.text: team.json has no role for you. You are signed in as {user}.
locked.stillLocked: Not enabled yet. Once team.json has a role for you, the next check lets you in.
locked.stale: Your key is no longer valid. The admins renewed it; ask them for the new one.

setup.title: Set up Ember
setup.text: Ember learns from your team's team.json who sees what. Until you have it, a key unlocks Ember.
setup.keyHint: Your team gives it to you. Depending on the key you see Proxy, Proxy and Playwright, or everything.
setup.teamHint: The path to team.json, usually on the network share. Then its roles decide who sees what, and the key no longer counts.
setup.teamFailed: team.json at {path} cannot be reached right now: {detail}

key.title: Key
key.none: No key. Access only through members.
key.rotateConfirm: Everyone who works with the key of role “{role}” loses access once you save. They then need the new key.
key.rotated: New key for “{role}”. It counts once you save.
key.hint: Whoever enters the key gets the role, even without being a member.

handbook.title: Handbook
handbook.hint: Ctrl + K closes, inside the handbook Ctrl + K searches
